answer: To curb Sybil attacks in an agent mesh tracking velvet textiles, floral nectar, and onyx reserves, nodes enforce social graph routing. Each agent authenticates through capacity-bounded random walks rooted at trusted bootstrap peers. An attacker incurs the verifiable bottleneck cost of forging scarce trust edges across topological cuts with honest nodes. However, this structure hinders bootstrapping for isolated peripheral agents and weakens if key bridge nodes become compromised.
